Troubleshooting

The symptoms people actually hit, each in the order worth checking. Everything below runs from a shell on the panel server, so none of it depends on the panel being reachable.

I lost the panel URL (the /random-path/ part)

The panel hides behind a random URL path; requests without it get an empty 404 page. That is normal behaviour, not a crash. The panel URL and the secret prefix are printed by:

The secret path is generated for you at install time and shown again on the Ready card. If you need a new one, set it in the panel under Settings → General → Panel URL Path and tick "I saved the new URL".

I forgot the owner password

The owner credential is a row in the panel's database, never a .env value. Reset it from the server; user data is untouched.

Both script forms restart the panel afterwards and wait for /health. The value is never echoed and never logged — it rides in the environment rather than in argv. Placeholder-looking passwords are refused, exactly as the panel refuses them.

Login fails with "username or password is incorrect"

  • Caps lock, or a trailing space — passwords are case-sensitive.
  • Logins are rate-limited per username and per address, with a Retry-After on the response. Restarting the panel does not clear the counters.
  • Still locked out? Use sudo ovmanager reset-password above.

The browser warns about the certificate

Expected with the self-signed default. The connection is encrypted; the browser just does not know who issued the certificate. Click Advanced, then Proceed. The warning disappears once you switch to Let's Encrypt with a real domain — see TLS certificates and sudo ovmanager tls.

ovmanager status or ovmanager logs report the panel unreachable

Rarely a certificate problem. The panel's health probe pins the certificate file declared in .env (SSL_CERTFILE) and only falls back to unverified behaviour when it cannot read that file, so a healthy self-signed panel reads as healthy. The hostname is not checked on purpose: the installer's certificate carries the public IP and has no SANs. What does fail the probe is a certificate on disk that does not match what the panel is actually serving — typically right after you replace it:

Node stays red

Check in this order:

#Check
1 Address. Public IP or hostname of the node, not a 10.x/192.168.x address.
2 Port. The sync API port (2083 by default), not the VPN port (1194).
3 API key. An exact copy with no extra spaces. sudo ovnode auth key reprints the name and key the panel needs.
4 TLS switch. It must match the node: selfsigned/le means on, none means off. A mismatch is a silent connection failure.
5 Name. The panel's node name must equal the node's OVN_NAME exactly.
6 Firewall. 2083/tcp reachable from the panel. Cloud security groups are the usual culprit.

From the node itself, this answers:

Subscription link shows localhost, or will not download

Subscription and download links are built from the address you opened the panel with. Always log in through the public URL. Behind a proxy where the request host is wrong, pin it: set PUBLIC_URL=https://panel.example.com in /opt/ovmanager/.env (or pass OVM_PUBLIC_URL at install time, or the base URL under Settings → Subscription Link), then restart the panel.

Reverse proxy issues: rate limiting or live telemetry freezing

  • All users rate-limited together: with Nginx, Caddy or Cloudflare in front, ensure TRUSTED_PROXY=true is set in /opt/ovmanager/.env. Without it, the panel sees the proxy IP as the client and shares login-failure counters across all users.
  • Live stats not updating: the live dashboard uses Server -Sent Events (SSE). If your reverse proxy buffers, the stream stalls. Disable buffering in the panel's location / block: proxy_buffering off; and proxy_read_timeout 300s;.

VPN connects but there is no internet

This is a node-side problem: IP forwarding and NAT.

  • Verify sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward is 1.
  • Make sure no firewall is blocking forwarding (nftables, cloud security group).
  • The node applies the forwarding rules itself on install; if ports changed, run sudo ovnode update.

On the node itself: unhealthy, or unreachable locally

From a shell on the VPN server:

  • If the local curl answers, the node is fine and the problem is network or firewall between the panel and the node — cloud security groups are the usual cause.
  • After changing ports or TLS, run sudo ovnode update, or reinstall with the same OVN_NAME — the data in /var/lib/ovnode/openvpn and /var/lib/ovnode is kept.

Installer errors

MessageWhat to do
Must run as root (sudo) Re-run with sudo.
systemd not found — native install needs it Use a full VM or a systemd-enabled server.
Port 80 is busy — Let's Encrypt standalone needs it Stop whatever listens on 80, or keep the self-signed certificate for now.
No verified release file is available The installer downloads a release binary from GitHub Releases. If that artifact is not published yet, nothing is wrong with your server — use a from-source install and upgrade later.
